Hot Chocolate from 1816 #christmas #hotchocolate 

Transcript of the video's audio (machine-made):
Throw out that powdered hot chocolate garbage because today we're making the real deal with a recipe from 1816 Welcome back to eats history today I'm making a German hot chocolate recipe from 1816 and let's learn a little bit of the history behind one of my favorite holiday drinks The history of hot chocolate begins in Mesoamerica where the cacao trees were cultivated by the Olmec Maya and later Aztecs It was consumed as a frothy drink mixed with water and spices And it was more of a sacred drink than a cozy holiday treat We get closer to our modern chocolate after the Spanish took cacao back to Europe and cooks began to add sugar Cinnamon and vanilla to soften its natural bitterness The drink was extremely expensive to make so it was only enjoyed by the Spanish elite But as the 17th century progressed its popularity and availability began to expand all across Europe And you saw chocolate houses open in the major cities at this point milk and cream began to be incorporated and the modern hot chocolate We know and love today was born the recipe I'm making today is from the 1816 German cookbook Noyesis Frankusius cookbook by md. Funk and it's a pretty normal hot chocolate recipe But it incorporates egg yolks to add a custardy depth to the drink. It's extremely rich But absolutely delicious if you're just used to the powdered stuff This one might actually blow you away. I'm giving it a 9.2 out of 10 and follow for more historical cooking
